title: What Software Architecture Actually Is
description: The high-level structure of a system and the decisions that are hard to change later.

title: Architecture vs Design vs Code
description: Three zoom levels of the same system, from broad structure down to individual lines.

title: Quality Attributes (the "-ilities")
description: Scalability, reliability, maintainability — the non-functional goals architecture actually serves.

title: Architectural Decision Records
description: Writing down why a major decision was made, so future you remembers the reasoning.

title: Identifying Architecture Stakeholders
description: The different people whose concerns an architecture has to satisfy at once.

title: Monolithic Architecture
description: One deployable unit containing the whole application.

title: Layered (N-Tier) Architecture
description: Organizing code into horizontal layers like presentation, business logic, and data.

title: Microservices Architecture
description: Splitting a system into small, independently deployable services.

title: Event-Driven Architecture
description: Services reacting to events instead of calling each other directly.

title: Service-Oriented Architecture
description: An earlier style of building systems from reusable, well-defined services.

title: Serverless Architecture
description: Running code as short-lived functions without managing the underlying servers.

title: Modular Monolith
description: A single deployable app with strict internal boundaries between its modules.

title: Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters) Architecture
description: Keeping core logic isolated from the outside world through defined ports.

title: Clean Architecture
description: Concentric layers where dependencies always point inward toward business rules.

title: Pipe-and-Filter Architecture
description: Data flowing through a chain of independent processing steps.

title: Separation of Concerns
description: Keeping distinct responsibilities in distinct, independent parts of a system.

title: Coupling and Cohesion
description: How tangled parts are with each other, and how focused each part is on its own job.

title: SOLID Principles Overview
description: Five widely referenced object-oriented design guidelines, in one quick pass.

title: Domain-Driven Design Basics
description: Modeling software around the real business domain and its own language.

title: Bounded Contexts
description: Drawing a clear boundary around where a specific model and its terms apply.

title: CQRS
description: Splitting the model used to read data from the model used to change it.

title: Event Sourcing
description: Storing every change as an event instead of just the current state.

title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Communication
description: Waiting for an immediate reply, versus firing something off and moving on.

title: REST API Design Basics
description: Resources, verbs, and status codes — the shape of a typical REST API.

title: Message Queues and Brokers
description: Passing messages between services through a durable middleman instead of directly.

title: API Gateways
description: One front door that routes, and often protects, requests to many backend services.

title: Service Discovery
description: How a service finds the current network address of another service automatically.

title: Database per Service vs Shared Database
description: Whether each service owns its own data, or several services share one database.

title: Consistency Models: Strong vs Eventual
description: Whether every reader sees the latest write immediately, or only eventually.

title: Caching Strategies
description: Storing a copy of data somewhere faster to reach than its original source.

title: The CAP Theorem
description: Why a distributed system can't fully guarantee consistency and availability during a network split.

title: Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling
description: Adding more machines, versus making one machine bigger.

title: Load Balancing Basics
description: Spreading incoming traffic across multiple servers instead of overloading one.

title: The Circuit Breaker Pattern
description: Stopping calls to a failing service temporarily instead of piling up more failures.

title: Retry and Backoff Strategies
description: Trying a failed request again, with growing delays instead of hammering it repeatedly.

title: Rate Limiting
description: Capping how many requests a client can make in a given window of time.

title: Observability: Logs, Metrics, Traces
description: The three main signals that let you understand what a running system is actually doing.

title: Security in Architecture
description: Designing access, boundaries, and trust into a system from the start, not bolted on later.

title: Documenting Architecture (the C4 Model)
description: Four zoom levels — context, container, component, code — for diagramming a system.

title: Making Architecture Trade-offs
description: Every architectural choice gains something and gives something up; naming that trade honestly.
